sample_unit: test CT images (40 with simulated artifacts plus 131 for correlation analysis)

links.outcome: OOD detection AUC for simulated CT artifacts, InfoOOD vs established OOD detectors
links.effect: InfoOOD AUC 0.93 vs 0.57 for embedded feature-based measures (strong rings artifact); AUC 0.75 vs 0.61 for reconstruction-based measure (weak sparse view artifact).
links.quote: TheInfoOODmeasure consistently outperformed the embedded feature-based measures in detecting OOD data (e.g. AUC = 0.93 vs. AUC = 0.57 for the strong rings artifact) and surpassed the reconstruction-based measure across weak magnitude artifacts (e.g., AUC = 0.75 vs. AUC = 0.61 for the weak sparse view artifact).

links.outcome: Segmentation performance under simulated low-dose, sparse-view, and ring artifacts
links.effect: Artifact simulation significantly degraded segmentation performance across all artifact types and magnitudes (p<0.001), worsening as magnitude increased.
links.quote: Artifact simulation significantly degraded segmentation model performance across all artifact types and magnitudes (ρ< 0.001), with model performance worsening as artifact magnitude increased.

screen.reason: Empirically develops and evaluates InfoOOD, a post hoc out-of-distribution (OOD) detection safeguard to identify corrupted or artifact-induced inputs before image segmentation failure.
